result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [ZeroInflatedPoisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) family for GAMLSS. twitter-card: title: >- [ZeroInflatedPoisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) family for GAMLSS. title: >- [ZeroInflatedPoisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) family for GAMLSS. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) family for GAMLSS. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L15-L322){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature ZeroInflatedPoisson() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Count data often has more zeros than a plain `Poisson` model can explain — for example, when some observations are structurally incapable of the event occurring at all (a "never-taker" always reports zero), in addition to the zeros that arise simply because the Poisson mean is low. `ZeroInflatedPoisson` models this as a mixture: with probability `pi` an observation is a structural zero, and with probability `1 - pi` it is drawn from an ordinary `Poisson(mu)` distribution (which can itself still produce a zero). Both `mu` and `pi` are modeled as smooth functions of covariates through `GAMLSS`, so the excess-zero probability and the count intensity can each vary independently across the covariate space. If overdispersion remains even among the non-structural-zero counts, use `ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial` instead. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Two distributional parameters are modeled, each with its own link: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \log(\mu), \qquad g_{\pi}(\pi) = \log\!\left(\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right). $$ The probability mass function is a mixture of a point mass at zero and a Poisson distribution: $$ P(Y = 0) = \pi + (1-\pi) e^{-\mu}, \qquad P(Y = k) = (1-\pi) \frac{\mu^{k} e^{-\mu}}{k!} \quad \text{for } k > 0. $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS for count data with excess zeros: ::: {#eb4c826e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.exp(0.5 + 0.4 * np.sin(x)) pi = expit(-1.0 + 0.8 * np.cos(x)) is_structural_zero = rng.uniform(size=n) < pi counts = rng.poisson(mu) y = np.where(is_structural_zero, 0, counts).astype(float) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "pi": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.ZeroInflatedPoisson(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: ZeroInflatedPoisson(mu=log, pi=logit) N obs: 300 Global deviance: 886.8940 AIC: 896.9039 BIC: 915.4410 Log-likelihood: -443.4470 Converged: True (6 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 2.00 Smooth 1: edf = 1.00 --- pi --- EDF total: 3.00 Smooth 1: edf = 2.00 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [parameter_names](#parameter_names){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Names of the distributional parameters modeled by this family. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [parameter_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the distributional parameters modeled by this family. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [parameter_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [d2l_dtheta2()](#d2l_dtheta2){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Compute the (negative) second derivative of the log-likelihood. | | [dl_dtheta()](#dl_dtheta){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Compute the first derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to a parameter. | | [initialize()](#initialize){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Generate starting values for `mu` and `pi` before the first IRLS iteration. | | [link()](#link){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Map a distributional parameter from its natural scale to the link scale. | | [link_derivative()](#link_derivative){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Compute the derivative of the link function with respect to the natural parameter. | | [link_inverse()](#link_inverse){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Map a distributional parameter from the link scale back to its natural scale. | | [log_likelihood()](#log_likelihood){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Compute the total log-likelihood under the zero-inflated Poisson model. | | [simulate()](#simulate){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Draw a random sample of counts from the fitted zero-inflated Poisson model. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the (negative) second derivative of the log-likelihood. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L199-L233){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature d2l_dtheta2( param, y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific working weight used by `GAMLSS`'s Fisher-scoring updates. The returned values approximate $-\partial^2 \ell / \partial \theta^2$ for `theta` in `{"mu", "pi"}`, computed separately for zero and positive observations to reflect the zero-inflated mixture, and floored at `_EPS` to keep weights strictly positive. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted values of all distributional parameters (`"mu"` and `"pi"`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weight for `param`. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the first derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to a parameter. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L157-L197){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature dl_dtheta( param, y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific score function used by `GAMLSS` to build the working response at each IRLS iteration. For zero observations the derivative accounts for the mixture weight of the point mass versus the Poisson component at zero; for positive observations it reduces to the ordinary Poisson score. For `mu` this is $\partial \ell / \partial \mu$, and for `pi` it is $\partial \ell / \partial \pi$, both derived from the zero-inflated Poisson log-likelihood. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to differentiate with respect to, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted values of all distributional parameters (`"mu"` and `"pi"`). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Generate starting values for `mu` and `pi` before the first IRLS iteration. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L268-L292){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Sets `mu` to the mean of the strictly positive observations (or 1.0 if none are positive) for every observation, and sets `pi` to half the observed fraction of zeros, clipped to `[0.01, 0.5]`, giving `GAMLSS` a reasonable starting point without any structural information about the covariates. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Initial values for `"mu"` and `"pi"`, each broadcast to the shape of `y`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Map a distributional parameter from its natural scale to the link scale. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L87-L108){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link( param, values, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies the parameter-specific link function used internally by `GAMLSS`: the log link $\eta = \log(\mu)$ for `mu` (clamped away from zero via `_MU_FLOOR`), and the logit link $\eta = \log(\pi / (1-\pi))$ for `pi` (clamped away from 0 and 1). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to transform, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Transformed values on the link (linear predictor) scale. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the derivative of the link function with respect to the natural parameter. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L132-L155){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_derivative( param, values, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Used by the IRLS fitting routine in `GAMLSS` to convert working responses between the link and natural scales. Returns $d\eta/d\mu = 1/\mu$ for `mu` and $d\eta/d\pi = 1/(\pi(1-\pi))$ for `pi`, both evaluated with the same clamping used in `link`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Derivative of the link function evaluated at `values`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Map a distributional parameter from the link scale back to its natural scale. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L110-L130){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_inverse( param, eta, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the inverse of `link`: $\mu = e^{\eta}$ (clipped to $[-30, 30]$ before exponentiating to avoid overflow) for `mu`, and $\pi = \mathrm{expit}(\eta)$ for `pi`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the parameter to transform, either `"mu"` or `"pi"`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values on the link scale. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values of `param` on its natural scale. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the total log-likelihood under the zero-inflated Poisson model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L235-L266){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature log_likelihood( y, params, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Evaluates $$ \ell = \sum_{i: y_i = 0} \log\!\big(\pi_i + (1-\pi_i) e^{-\mu_i}\big) + \sum_{i: y_i > 0} \Big[\log(1-\pi_i) + y_i \log(\mu_i) - \mu_i - \log(y_i!)\Big], $$ summing the point-mass contribution for structural zeros with the Poisson contribution for observed counts. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"` for each observation. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Draw a random sample of counts from the fitted zero-inflated Poisson model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/zero_inflated.py#L294-L319){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( params, rng, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each observation, flips a `pi`-weighted coin to decide whether it is a structural zero; observations that are not structural zeros are drawn from `Poisson(mu)`, so a sampled value can still be zero even when it was not selected as a structural zero. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict of str to NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted values of `"mu"` and `"pi"` for each observation to simulate. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [object]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Random number generator exposing `uniform` and `poisson` methods, such as a `numpy.random.Generator`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, one per row of `params`. :::
